COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1080 of 2025
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State.
3. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
respondent no. 2.
4. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for 
Union of India / respondent no. 3.
5. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, (through V.C.) learned 
counsel for the respondent no. 4. 
6. Petitioner institution gave admission to 26 
students, NEET qualified without any counselling, 
though as per directions of the Central Government 
admission should be done only after counselling.
7. Learned counsel for the University Mr. Sandeep 
Kothari submits that since the admission to these 26 
students were given without counselling, therefore, 
these 26 students cannot be enrolled in the University 
and they cannot be permitted to participate in the 
examination. 
8. In response to this, learned counsel for the 
petitioner argued that though 26 students were given 
admission without any counselling, but they are 
studying since last 2 years, therefore, keeping in view 
the future prospects of 26 students, they may be 
enrolled provisionally in the University and permitted 
provisionally to participate in the examination. 
9. Now, the question is - if the admissions of 26 
students are without counselling whether they can be 
enrolled in the University and be permitted to appear 
in the examination. This aspect requires to be 
scrutinized. Further taking into consideration the fact 
that the students are NEET qualified and studying 
since last two years, in such an eventuality, if they are 
not enrolled in University and they are not 
provisionally permitted to appear in the examination 
certainly it will affect the future prospect of the 26 
students.  10. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
University submits that only the institution approached 
this Court and if there is genuine grievance then that 
can be looked into in a petition filed by those 26 
students. 
11. Here the only issue is with regard to the 
enrolment of 26 students, who are NEET qualified, 
admitted in the institution petitioner without 
counselling. 
12. List on 23.04.2025.
13. By that time, learned counsel for the University 
may get instructions in the matter. 
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 16.04.2025.
SKS

Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Navneet Kaushik and Mr. Niranjan Bhatt,
learned counsel for the petitioners. 
2. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
respondents. 
3. Mr. Saurav Adhikari and Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned 
counsel for the Union of India. 
4. The facts, in brief, are that the petitioners are 
students of respondent no.3-College; that, the admissions 
were forwarded to the University and the National 
Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has 
approved the admissions; that, now, when the time for 
taking up examinations have arrived and hall tickets were 
sought, the University has stalled the process of 
consideration on the ground that the students have not 
participated in the counselling; that, the university does 
not dispute the fact that they had participated in the NEET 
examination and the University also does not dispute the 
fact that they have secured marks above the stipulated cut￾off marks of 50% or so, and that they are fully qualified to 
be admitted. 
5. The fact remains that the admissions are against 
seats that have not been filled up during the counselling. 
6. In view of the twin facts that the students have 
participated in the NEET examination and are part of the 
merit list prepared by the National Testing Agency (NTA),  which conducts the NEET examination and, in view of the 
fact, that they possessed all the requisite qualification to be 
admitted into the course. We are of the considered opinion 
that technicality of non-approval of the University, which 
needs to be gone into after a full-fledged hearing, the 
academic career of the students should not be jeopardised 
and, hence, pending disposal of the writ petitions, we 
direct the University to issue hall tickets and permit the 
petitioners/ students to take up the examination, subject to 
the final orders in the writ petition. It is made clear that the 
result of the examination shall not be announced without 
the concurrence of this Court. 
7. Copy of this order be forwarded to the concerned 
Registrar of the University forthwith. 
8. List this case on 09.09.2025. 
(Alok Mahra, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 18.07.2025 18.07.2025

Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned 
counsel for the petitioners.
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing 
Counsel for the Union of India.
3. Mr. Devendra Pant, learned 
Standing Counsel for the State.
4. Ms. Abhilasha Tomar, proxy counsel 
for Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel 
for respondent no.2.
5. Mr. Gaurav Nayal proxy counsel for 
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for 
respondent no.4.
6. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel 
for the intervener through Video 
Conferencing.
7. Since all these petitions raise 
identical issues concerning the 
dispute relating to admission to the 
B.A.M.S. course for academic sessions 
2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024 
and 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, they 
are being heard together.
8. Learned counsel appearing for the 
petitioners submits that the present writ 
petitions have been filed seeking a  direction to respondent no. 2 to enroll 
the students admitted by the petitioners’ 
college and to permit such students to 
appear in their practical as well as 
semester examinations of the B.A.M.S. 
course.
9. Learned counsel further submits 
that admission to the B.A.M.S. course 
was made subject to qualification in the 
National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test 
(NEET) pursuant to the Central 
Government Notification/Regulation 
dated 07.12.2018, whereby NEET was 
prescribed as a mandatory eligibility 
criterion for admission to the said 
course. It is submitted that NEET was 
introduced for the first time for the 
academic session 2018–2019, which led 
to the filing of several writ petitions 
across the country challenging the 
imposition of NEET as an essential 
qualification for admission to the 
B.A.M.S. course. The controversy 
ultimately reached the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, which, in Association of 
Managements of Homeopathic Medical 
Colleges of Maharashtra v. Union of 
India & Ors., (2019) 20 SCC 511, held 
that for the academic session 2018–
2019, qualification in NEET was not an 
essential requirement for admission to 
the B.A.M.S. course. Thereafter, in 
subsequent civil appeals, the Hon’ble 
Apex Court relaxed the condition of 
mandatory NEET qualification and 
permitted students, who were otherwise 
eligible, to continue their studies for the 
academic sessions 2019–2020 and 2020–
2021. It is submitted that while most 
such students have already completed 
the course, a few are still pursuing their 
studies. 10. Learned counsel for the petitioners 
further submits that the students 
involved in the present writ petitions 
were earlier permitted to appear in the 
examinations pursuant to interim orders
passed by this Hon’ble Court. It is 
further submitted that the students have 
qualified the NEET examination and 
possess the minimum prescribed 
eligibility and requisite percentage as 
mandated under the applicable 
regulations.
11. Learned counsel further submits 
that the next practical and semester 
examinations are scheduled to be held 
on 27.01.2026. Therefore, a prayer is 
made that the students of the petitioners’ 
college be permitted to appear in the said 
examinations.
12. In view of the aforesaid facts and 
circumstances, and purely in the interest 
of justice, the rest of students admitted 
during the Academic Sessions 2021-
2022, 2022-2023 and 2023-2024 and 
2025-2026, who have qualified the NEET 
examination and fulfill the minimum 
prescribed eligibility and percentage, are 
provisionally permitted to appear in the 
examination scheduled to be held on 
27.01.2026, subject to the final decision
in the present writ petitions.
13. List the case in due course.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) Vacation Judge
23.01.2026
Mamta
